title: Record edit dialog: on a row the caller may read but not write (sharing / RLS / ownership), the fields are offered as editable and the save is refused whole — the dialog never asks whether the row is writable
body:
Filing gate: ① a client advertises an edit that the gate refuses. Measured by the dev on PR #27137 (#26594, PR 2; os-dev-report 6463775639). Filed by `domain:spec` seat 3 · `os-support-ai` · session `session_01WGufzgbJhFoXYsLSe5WSPP`. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets the lane and the grade (the ui lane is suggested).

**Business reason.** Two caller states hit this:
- a caller who may read a record but not write it, because sharing, row-level security or ownership leaves the row outside their write scope;
- a caller who may write some rows of the object, and so holds the object grant.

For both, the console's record edit dialog still opens with the fields enabled. The user fills them in, presses Save, and the server refuses the whole update. The permission contract promises that "a client never advertises an edit the gate refuses" (`packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts`, the `when` description). For field-level locks, ruling B on #26594 now keeps that promise. For row-level write scope, nothing does.

## Measured (dev, on PR #27137's head `90f1ea4dfc`)

- `managedModeLocked` in `ui/packages/plugin-form/src/fieldWriteGate.ts` reads the object grant only. Nothing in the dialog (`ModalForm`, `ObjectForm`, `DrawerForm`) gates on record-level edit permission.
- On a `public_read` row the caller may read, `PATCH` refuses the update as a whole, yet `GET /api/v1/data/:object/:id/field-access` lists `title` and `summary` as `editable`. That is by contract: `editable` is field-level only and leaves out the object grant and the row-level write scope (sharing, RLS, ownership). The dogfood leg in `record-field-access-when.dogfood.test.ts` pins this (8/8).
- This behaviour predates PR #27137. That PR documents it in the ui `RecordFieldAccess` type, the scope's doc and `field-level-security.mdx`, and does not change it.

## Wanted (for triage to grade and route)

The record edit surfaces (the edit dialog, the record page's Edit action, and inline edit if it applies) should ask the server whether this row is writable by this caller, and not offer the edit when it is not. The answer must be the gate's own judgement, never a second client-side evaluator. One option is to widen the record-scoped answer with a row-level `writable` flag. Another is to reuse an existing server answer for row write scope, if one exists; measure that first. Precedent for a lock of this kind: #25934 (pending-approval `lockRecord`, offered inline edit, answered 409).

## Dedupe

`search_issues` on this repo, "record edit dialog offers fields on a row the caller cannot write sharing record-level edit permission save refused", returned #26594 (the source; field-level only), #25934 (closed; the approval-lock shape, not row write scope) and unrelated dialog cards (#26891, #26888). **New.**
